sentences.text: 2. Application U/s 482 No. 18220 of 2022 has been filed by the applicant for quashing the charge sheet dated 23.10.2021, under Sections 366, 376, 342 I.P.C. arising out of Case Crime No. 268 of 2021, Police Station Sikandrarau, District Hathras.

3. Heard Sri Mahesh Kumar, learned counsel for the revisionist / applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and Sri Lal Ji Pandey & Ms. Abha Pandey, learned counsel appearing on behalf of opposite party nos. 2 & 3.
4.

Brief facts of the case are that the opposite party no. 2 had lodged a first information report on 22.06.2021 with the allegation that the accused-revisionist has enticed away her daughter on 21.06.2021.
The case was registered as Case Crime No. 268 of 2021, under Sections 366 I.P.C. in Police Station Sikandrarau, District Hathras.
The victim was recovered after about three months on 24.09.2021.

The Investigating Officer has recorded the statement of victim under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
on 24.09.2021, in which she has supported the case of prosecution and has stated that she went with the revisionist on 21.07.2021 to Allahabad.
It is further stated that the revisionist on the basis of some photographs has blackmailed the victim and she under the fear has went with the revisionist.

The subsequent statement of victim was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. on 29.09.2021 in which she has stated that she is aged about 20 years and she went with the revisionist under the fear as she was blackmailed by the revisionist on the basis of some photographs.

Thereafter, the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. on 30.09.2021, in which she again supported the prosecution case that she was blackmailed by the revisionist and she went to Allahabad with the revisionist under the fear.

The Investigating Officer has recorded the statement of informant and other witnesses who have also supported the prosecution case, has submitted charge sheet against the revisionist under Sections 342, 366 and 376 I.P.C. on 23.10.2021.
The learned Magistrate had summoned the revisionist to face trial.

5. The revisionist, who is applicant in Application U/s 482 No. 18220 of 2022 has filed aforesaid application for quashing the charge sheet dated 23.10.2021.
6.

During pendency of trial as well as Application U/s 482 No. 18220 of 2022, the revisionist had moved an application under Section 227 Cr.P..C.on 23.05.2023 for discharge on the ground that the revisionist has not committed any offence as alleged in the first information report.
The victim is major aged about 20 years and she is consenting party and they solemnized marriage in temple.

The revisionist had approached to the Hon'ble High Court and a joint writ petition has been filed by the revisionist and victim being Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 4907 of 2021 (Sumit Kumar @ Bablu and another vs. State of U.P. and another) for quashing of first information report of Case Crime No.
268 of 2021.

sentences.text: Since the victim is major and was consenting party, no offence against the revisionist is made out and the revisionist is liable to be discharged from the offences.

7. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of opposite party nos. 2 and 3 submits that the statement of victim was recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. in which she has supported the prosecution case and has stated that she went with the revisionist under the fear, as her photographs were with the revisionist and she was blackmailed by the revisionist on the basis of such photographs.
Admittedly, the revisionist is a married person having two children.
The revisionist being married person has enticed away the victim and as such, he has committed offence under Section 376 I.P.C.
The discharge application filed by the revisionist was rightly rejected by the learned trial court by order dated 17.06.2023 and there is no illegality or irregularity in any manner.

Lastly, it is submitted that the trial court after considering the entire evidence and materials which were collected by the Investigating Officer during investigation has found a prima-facie case against the revisionist and has rightly rejected the discharge application filed by the revisionist.

8. Considered the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

For ready reference Section 227 Cr.P.C. is quoted herein below:-
"227. Discharge.

If, upon consideration of the record of the case and the documents submitted therewith, and after hearing the submissions of the accused and the prosecution in this behalf, the Judge considers that there is not sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused, he shall discharge the accused and record his reasons for so doing."
10. From bare perusal of Section 227 Cr.P.C., that if upon consideration of Police report and documents collected during investigation and after hearing accused as well as prosecution the Court found that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused, the Court can discharge the accused.

The approach to be adopted by the Court while exercising the power of discharge is considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Onkar Nath Mishra and others Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, 2008 2 SCC 561.

entities.text: Onkar Nath Mishra and others Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, 2008 2 SCC 561
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraph No.11 is quoted herein below:-
"11.

It is trite that at the stage of framing of charge the court is required to evaluate the material and documents on record with a view to finding out if the facts emerging therefrom, taken at their face value, disclosed the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence.
At that stage, the court is not expected to go deep into the probative value of the material on record.
What needs to be considered is whether there is a ground for presuming that the offence has been committed and not a ground for convicting the accused has been made out.

At that stage, even strong suspicion founded on material which leads the court to form a presumptive opinion as to the existence of the factual ingredients constituting the offence alleged would justify the framing of charge against the accused in respect of the commission of that offence."

3 11.

entities.text: Sumit Kumar @ Bablu vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble apex Court in the case of State of Tamil Nadu Vs. N. Suresh Rajan and others reported in 2014 (11) SCC 709, has held that at the time of deciding the application for discharge,
the Court is not expected to go deep into the matter and consider the entire evidence and material which are available on record.

entities.text: State of Tamil Nadu Vs. N. Suresh Rajan and others reported in 2014 (11) SCC 709
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraph 29 is quoted below:-
"29.
We have bestowed our consideration to the rival submissions and the submissions made by Mr. Ranjit Kumar commend us.

True it is that at the time of consideration of the applications for discharge, the court cannot act as a mouthpiece of the prosecution or act as a post-office and may sift evidence in order to find out whether or not the allegations made are groundless so as to pass an order of discharge.

It is trite that at the stage of consideration of an application for discharge,
the court has to proceed with an assumption that the materials brought on record by the prosecution are true and evaluate the said materials and documents with a view to find out whether the facts emerging therefrom taken at their face value disclose the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence.

At this stage,
probative value of the materials has to be gone into and the court is not expected to go deep into the matter and hold that the materials would not warrant a conviction.
In our opinion, what needs to be considered is whether there is a ground for presuming that the offence has been committed and not whether a ground for convicting the accused has been made out.

To put it differently, if the court thinks that the accused might have committed the offence on the basis of the materials on record on its probative value, it can frame the charge; though for conviction, the court has to come to the conclusion that the accused has committed the offence.
The law does not permit a mini trial at this stage."

12. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of M.P. vs. Mohanlal Soni reported in (2000) 6 SCC 338 has held that at the time of framing of charges the Court has to prima facie consider whether there is sufficient ground against the accused or not and the Court is not required to consider the evidence in detail and appreciate evidence to conclude that there are sufficient materials for conviction of the accused.

entities.text: State of M.P. vs. Mohanlal Soni reported in (2000) 6 SCC 338
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Only prima facie satisfaction of learned trial court is required at the time of framing of charges.

Relevant paragraph 7 is quoted herein below:-
"7.
The crystallized judicial view is that at the stage of framing charge, the court has to prima facie consider whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

The court is not required to appreciate evidence to conclude whether the materials produced are sufficient or not for convicting the accused."
13.

It is well settled law by Hon'ble Supreme Court in series of cases that at the time of framing of charges the Court has to prima facie consider whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused or not.

The Court is not required to appreciate the evidence and materials,
which are available on record to reach at the conclusion for convicting the accused.
If the Court is satisfied that a prima facie case is made out against the accused and there is sufficient ground for proceeding further, then the charges are to be framed.

sentences.text:
From the record, it is apparent that the first information report was lodged by opposite party no.
3 with the allegation that her daughter was enticed away by the revisionist.

The victim in her statement recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. has clearly stated that on the basis of some photographs, she was blackmailed by revisionist and she went with the revisionist to Allahabad under the fear and rape was committed by the revisionist.

The Investigating Officer after due investigation had found that the revisionist is a married person having two children and the victim was enticed away under the fear and there is specific allegation against the revisionist to commit rape with the victim, had submitted charge sheet under Sections 366, 376, 342 I.P.C,.
15.

The discharge application filed by accused-revisionist was rejected by the learned Sessions Judge by a detailed order after prima-facie satisfaction that there is sufficient evidence and material against the accused-revisionist for framing charge under Sections 366, 376, 342 I.P.C.
16.

Learned counsel for the revisionist has failed to point out any illegality or infirmity in the impugned order rejecting the discharge application.
17. No ground for quashing of charge sheet as well as discharge of revisionist / applicant is made out.
The Application U/s 482 and Criminal Revision are devoid of merits and are liable to be dismissed.
18. The criminal revision as well as Application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. are dismissed accordingly.
Interim order, if any, stands discharged.
